subject: Information Theory
title: Entropy vs Thermodynamic Entropy
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Entropy vs Thermodynamic Entropy.

hook.text: Physicists had entropy long before Shannon. Boltzmann carved it on a tombstone. Are they the same thing?

buildup.text: Thermodynamic entropy measures molecular disorder. Shannon entropy measures information uncertainty.

discovery.text: Both use the same mathematical form: a sum of probabilities times their logarithms. Coincidence? Not quite.

twist.text: Jaynes showed in 1957 that thermodynamic entropy is Shannon entropy applied to physics. Same math, different domain.

climax.text: Von Neumann told Shannon to call it entropy because nobody understands it—so he'd win every argument.

punchline.text: Same formula. Physics and communication connected.

quiz.question: How are Shannon entropy and thermodynamic entropy related?
options: They share the same mathematical form
One is the inverse of the other
